doc: Denon/Marantz telnet control protocol grammar.
This data file is the ONLY place that contains fixed wire tokens (such as
PSBAS for bass or the enum values OFF/LOW/MID/HI/AUTO). It exists because a
receiver does not publish its own wire vocabulary: it describes controls by
functional names (ToneControl, DynamicCompression, ...) and by display names,
ranges, steps and option labels, but never says 'bass is sent as PSBAS'. That
linkage is the Denon protocol itself and is identical across all Denon and
Marantz models.
Everything device specific (which controls actually exist, their display
names, numeric ranges, option labels, the channel list, the source list and
renames, visibility) is discovered at runtime from the receiver and is NEVER
stored here. The engine builds an entity for a control only when the receiver
advertises the matching capability AND this profile knows how to speak to it.
For enum controls, 'values' lists the wire tokens in the canonical protocol
order. The engine pairs them, by position, with the ordered display labels the
receiver publishes. When the counts differ it falls back to the wire tokens as
labels so a mismatch can never cause a wrong command to be sent.

sound_mode_wire_overrides.doc: Deterministic display-name -> MS wire token map for modes whose wire token differs from the upper-cased display name. These tokens were observed live from the receiver (it reports them via MS). For every other mode the upper-cased display name is used. This is the robust base; adaptive learning (optional) can add more at runtime.

sound_mode_genre_commands.doc: How to switch the receiver to a sound mode genre group. Keyed by the genre code the receiver uses (from OPSMLALL/SSSMG); the value is the MS command token. Verified live: MOVIE/MUSIC/GAME work; the Pure group needs 'PURE DIRECT' (plain 'PURE' does not). This is fixed protocol grammar; the codes and display names still come from the device.

doc: Maps the receiver's speaker group codes (from the SSSPC introspection) to
channel codes, so only speakers that are actually configured get channel
entities. Which groups are present is discovered from SSSPC; this map is
just the fixed protocol grammar linking a group to its channels. A group
is treated as absent when any of its SSSPC lines carries the absent token.
How zones are addressed on the wire. The NUMBER and names of zones are
discovered from the receiver (DeviceZones); only the addressing grammar is
fixed here. The main zone uses the core controls (ZM/MV/MU/SI). Every
additional zone N uses the prefix 'Z<N>' (Z2, Z3, ...), which is overloaded
for power, volume, mute and source; the parser disambiguates by content.

source_names.doc: One line per input: 'SSFUN<CODE> <display name>'. Provides the SI source code and the (possibly renamed) display name.

source_visibility.doc: One line per input: 'SSSOD<CODE> USE|DEL'. Marks which sources the user kept visible.

channel_levels.doc: One line per configured channel: 'SSLEV<CODE> <level>' terminated by 'SSLEV END'. Reveals which channels are actually configured.

speaker_config.doc: One line per speaker group with its size/presence setting.

sound_mode_group.doc: Reports the receiver's current sound mode genre group directly (MOV/MUS/GAM/PUR).

quick_select_names.doc: Main zone quick select preset names, one per line ('SSQSNZMAQS<n> <name>'), terminated by 'SSQSNZMA END'.

quick_select.doc: Currently recalled main zone quick select preset number (0 = none/modified).

sound_mode_list.doc: OPSMLALL lists every available sound mode across all genres (Movie/Music/Game/Pure), one per line, terminated by 'OPSMLALL END'. Used for the full flat set and the per genre groups.

current_sound_modes.doc: OPSML lists the modes actually selectable in the CURRENT context/group, terminated by 'OPSML END'. Context aware: includes modes OPSMLALL omits (such as Auto) and marks the selected mode. Drives the sound mode select for the active group.

sample_rate.name: Sample Rate
sample_rate.doc: Sample rate token such as '48K'. 'NON' means no active signal.

decoder.name: Decoder
decoder.doc: Active decoder/audio format, for example 'PCM' (space padded).

mode_info.name: Mode Info
mode_info.doc: Informational mode string, for example 'Stereo' (space padded).

system_power.doc: System standby power. Distinct from the main zone power.

main_volume.doc: Master volume. Two/three digit half step scale, 80 == 0 dB reference.

main_source.doc: Main zone input source. Codes and names are discovered via SSFUN/SSSOD.

sound_mode.doc: Surround / sound mode. Selectable values are learned from what the receiver reports.

bass.doc: Tone control bass. Half step level, 50 == 0 dB.

treble.doc: Tone control treble. Half step level, 50 == 0 dB.

lfe.doc: LFE level, 0 down to -10 dB. The receiver does not publish this range (its LFE block is empty), so the protocol defined range is given here as a fallback.

reference_level_offset.doc: Calibration reference level offset in dB.

cinema_eq.doc: Cinema EQ. Note the embedded '.' in the wire token.

subwoofer_level.doc: Subwoofer level, half step, 50 == 0 dB. The dB range is discovered from the receiver's SubwooferLevel block.

sleep_timer.doc: Sleep timer in minutes ('OFF' when disabled). The receiver does not publish a range (its SleepTimer block is empty), so the protocol defined range is given here as a fallback.

dts_neural_x.doc: DTS Neural:X upmixer. Verified live (PSNEURAL ON/OFF). Only applies to compatible content.

tcp_client_lfc.doc: Calibration Low Frequency Containment. Verified live (PSLFC ON/OFF).

effect_level.doc: DSP effect level (matrix/DSP sound modes). Verified live (PSEFF). The receiver publishes only step/default, so 0-15 is the protocol fallback range. Only applies in DSP modes.

containment_amount.doc: Calibration LFC containment amount. Verified live (PSCNTAMT). The receiver publishes only step/default, so 0-7 is the protocol fallback range. Applies when Calibration LFC is on.

audio_delay.doc: Audio delay in milliseconds. The receiver does not publish a range, so the protocol range (0-200 ms) is used as a fallback.

dialog_control.doc: Dialog Control level 0-6. The receiver publishes only the step and default, so the 0-6 range is the protocol fallback.

video_mode.doc: Video processing mode. Wire values verified live (AUTO/GAME/MOVI); labels come from Deviceinfo. Only changeable with an active video signal.

hdmi_video_output.doc: HDMI monitor output selection. Wire values verified live (AUTO/1/2).

aspect_ratio.doc: Video aspect ratio. Wire values verified live (FUL=16:9, NRM=4:3).

input_mode.doc: Audio input mode for the current source (how audio is received). This is the eARC/ARC selector for the TV Audio source. EARC verified live (the source stayed locked to the active eARC signal, so the other values could not be cycle-verified); the rest are the documented Denon SD tokens. Order matches the Deviceinfo Input Mode list.

channel_level.doc: Per channel volume trim. Configured channels, their names and their dB ranges are all discovered from the receiver; live trims are read/written via CV<code>.
